summary: This Hannibal/Rome lecture is already public Strategy evidence for a story becoming material capacity; its remaining corpus impact is to keep Roman no-surrender, history-as-religion, liberty-as-law, and devotion-as-sacrifice routed across Strategy, Nation, Civilization, and Legitimacy without creating a standalone Rome or Hannibal page.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Rome wins because character and value system convert into repeated shipbuilding, manpower replacement, discipline, and refusal to surrender after Cannae.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Strategy page already cites this source in the Rome section as the ancient counterexample where story passes the material test. No episode read JSON link is changed in this intake because the page does not yet expose a specific Rome/no-surrender lens-point anchor.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this source as the Rome case showing that a story is not automatically fantasy. Roman piety, liberty, citizenship, and no surrender become material capacity because institutions, manpower, repetition, discipline, and endurance carry the story through defeat.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Strategy owns Rome only where belief meets economics, organization, logistics, replacement capacity, and battlefield adaptation. It should not become a Roman-history page.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold Roman liberty-as-law, republic-over-king obedience, and all-or-nothing devotion as premodern comparison pressure for the nation-state machine: a collective body becomes more real than family, safety, or individual survival.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Nation receives this only as a comparative ancestor of sacred collective-body formation. Strategy remains the home for the Hannibal/Cannae material test, and Civilization owns the wider inner order.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the lecture only in future civilization synthesis if the page needs a martial inner-order contrast: Rome turns history into mythology and religion, making violence, law, liberty, family sacrifice, and survival cohere into a lived world.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Civilization owns the inner arrangement of religion, memory, violence, law, and survival. It should not absorb the whole Hannibal military case.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Keep the Brutus and Roman-history passages available for future comparison with Legitimacy Fiction only where founding stories make obedience to an impersonal republic feel rightful enough to override family and ordinary morality.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Legitimacy owns rightful obedience and founding-memory authority. Strategy owns the war-capacity result; Nation owns collective-body devotion.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold the 'what matters is what they believed' passage as story-control pressure only when a future synthesis compares historical truth with belief that makes a people act.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Stories owns belief as reality-making. Strategy owns the proof that the belief survives contact with ships, food, armies, and time.

chronology_notes.note: On 2024-11-07 Jiang gives the Roman counterexample now used by the public Strategy page: story can pass the material test when character, institutions, manpower, discipline, and logistics make no-surrender belief executable after catastrophe.
The same lecture gives a martial inner-order formulation: Roman history becomes mythology and religion, and that sacred memory organizes violence, law, liberty, family sacrifice, and survival.
Roman devotion appears as an older comparison layer for collective-body formation before the modern nation-state: liberty means obedience to law and history, and devotion means all or nothing.

next_actions.action: Do not create standalone Hannibal, Carthage, Roman No Surrender, Roman Liberty, Lucius Brutus, Cult Of Rome, History As Religion, Cannae, or Rome War Machine pages from this source alone. Route each pressure point by active mechanism.

If public synthesis follows, prefer a Strategy replacement/compression note around Rome-as-material-capacity or a Civilization/Nation comparison note around sacred civic memory; do not reopen the settled Strategy split decision from this source alone.

If provenance maintenance follows, first add a durable Strategy lens point for Rome/no-surrender material capacity or link the episode read only after such an anchor exists; the current public page cites the source inline but exposes no specific Rome anchor.

If future concept work tests a held civic-history-as-sacred-war-machine seed, compare this source against Nation unity-of-will, Legitimacy founding-memory authority, Civilization inner-order religion, and Strategy war-form material tests before promotion.
